text.p: - A bomb, placed in front of the house of a Slovenian judge in the city of Miklavz on Tuesday, seriously injured the judge's wife.
- Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek signed a United Nations anti-nuclear agreement in New York on Tuesday.

- Slovenia is currently involved in two court cases trying to achieve a permanent freeze of the assets of the former Yugoslavia in commercial banks in Cyprus and France. Slovenia hopes the assets would remain frozen until the succession talks of the former Yugoslav states end.
- The parliament continues its debate on how to carry out the electoral referendum set for December 8, which will include three different proposals for a new election system.
- According to UNCTAD's report on foreign investment, Slovenia ranks fifth among the former socialist countries with $88 of foreign investment per capita in 1995.
- Slovenian electricity producers say they will face losses this year due to low electricity prices.
- Economic ministers of Slovenia and the Netherlands signed an agreement on promotion of mutual investments.
- The construction of a waste water cleaning facility in Ljubljana, begun in 1989, has not been completed due to a lack of money.
